correctness.rationale: Every orbit is a feasible coordinate-count quadruple. A concrete pointwise-stabilizer subgroup acts transitively on these quadruples. The two root-distances and an exactly countable common-distance-decreasing neighbour statistic f=delta reconstruct the quadruple; equitability with both singleton roots makes all three invariants stable-class constants, and automorphism invariance supplies the converse. Non-equitability outside q=2 or t=1 or t=d is certified for every parameter by two explicit feasible profiles with pair (2,t) but f=0 versus 1. One pass from two-distance cells sees f. Three independently coded scripts and their actual outputs verify 82 direct graphs, 1026 quotient graphs, and 2646 parameter regimes; these are not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exact equality between 1-WL stable colours and pointwise automorphism-stabilizer orbits for arbitrary Hamming dimensions, alphabet sizes and two-root distances is a uniform structural result. It provides class-count and class-size formulas and a sharp q=2/t=1/t=d trichotomy for when metric pairs are sufficient, with a universally defined defect invariant and one-round remedy in all other parameters. It explains which local data recover genuine graph symmetry, beyond a routine isolated small example.
